newsitem.title: UK: M&S no plans to enter food loyalty fray.
newsitem.headline: M&S no plans to enter food loyalty fray.

text.p: British retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Tuesday it would not join the fight for customer loyalty raging between the UK's major food superstores by introducing loyalty cards or offering discounts.

M&S acknowledged the UK food business was fiercely competitive and that there was currently massive price deflation partly as a result of the strong pound. But the group maintained margins last year and held market share, which it estimated at around three or four percent.
Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said M&S's food business was slightly different from that of the mainstream stores such as Tesco Plc and J.Sainsbury Plc.
"We're not in the loyalty or discount business," he told a news conference, "It's not the way we've ever done business and I don't see why we should start."
Guy McCracken, managing director of the food division, said M&S's strengths in food came from product development, such as chilled ready meals, where the company has around 50 percent of the market.
An M&S food department carried approximately 2,500 lines, while a large food retailer -- such as Tesco or Sainsbury -- would typically stock some 20,000 different products, he said.
Greenbury said all the evidence had shown that M&S's customers were loyal already and appreciated what the company had to offer in food.
The retailer reported food sales growth had slowed to 4.5 percent in the second half of its 1996/97 year, from 6.7 percent in the first half.
Food price inflation fell to one percent in the second half from three in the first half, but was currently running at minus one percent, finance director Robert Colvill told journalists.
"In the face of strong promotional efforts from the larger food groups, we have maintained level margins during the year and retained our competitive position," he said.

Greenbury said the price deflation was unlikely to last. He said M&S's food market share was not likely to change dramatically, but it's share of Britain's 60 billion stg food market was nevertheless important.
Food accounts for about 40 percent of M&S's total UK sales.

Earlier M&S reported an 11 percent increase in annual profits to 1.1 billion stg, but worries about its performance in food hit its shares and contributed to profit forecast downgrades. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
